steps.text: In a small bowl, blend the sour cream and baking soda, and set aside.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a large baking sheet.

In a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, cream of tartar, and salt. Cut in the butter. Stir the sour cream mixture and egg into the flour mixture until just moistened. Mix in the raisins.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface, and knead briefly. Roll or pat dough into a 3/4 inch thick round. Cut into 12 wedges, and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes in the preheated oven, until golden brown on the bottom.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma Johnson's Scones
raw_recipe.description: Using simple ingredients and only 30 minutes, this easy raisin scone recipe is a perfect sweet snack for the whole family.

review.reviewBody:
Great recipe, just a few tips to avoid dryness and any disaster.

1. Combine the sour cream (make sure you use sour cream) and baking soda, set aside.
2. Mix the butter (make sure it is at room temperature) with the sugar (I just use 3/4 cup),
3. Beat the egg with vanilla (yes, I add 1 tsp. of vanilla)
4. Add the beaten egg to the sugar/butter mixture. 
5. Add the sour cream with baking soda and mix until smooth and creamy.
6. Mix well the dry ingredients and then add them to the wet mixture, just to get everything together, do not over mix.

From here, you can add as many "toppings" as you want. This are tried and tested:
Chocolate chips
Craisins, raisings, cherries, etc.
Dried fruits such as apricots, figs or prunes (chopped in little pieces)
Nuts (chopped in little pieces)

I make 16 balls and press them w/ my hands to make a flat circle. Bake for 15 min. 
The secret with these scones is to not over mix or over handle.

I've made this recipe MANY Times now. It's a wonderful basic recipe, but I found the butter I use really makes a difference. Regular butter creates a crumblier scone, and organic unsalted makes it more cake-like, like a Starbucks scone. I prefer it that way. My favorite flavors so far are Orange Spice (orange extract, grated orange rind, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg and ginger), and lemon currant (lemon extract, lemon rind, currants). My husband's favorite is regular chocolate chip. I always break the batter in half and make 2 different flavors. Then I divide each flavor into half and make 2 rounds. If I only do 1 round per flavor, the scones are very large (Starbucks size). I prefer them smaller, so I don't eat so much at each sitting!! They are PERFECT with hot tea. I like the orange spice with lady grey, and lemon currant with green tea. OH! I also glaze the scones with a glaze made of orange or lemon extract and powdered sugar. So yummy and so pretty!

Fabulous! Simple, they were perfect with my first try! My sister shared this recipe with me a few months ago, I had tried several other recipes and never could get one to work. This is now my go to recipe. I have begun experimenting with different fruits and now also using the suggestion to freeze them before baking. So delicious to have fresh scones in just a few minutes. 

One change we both make is to use a 2 1/4 “ round cookie cutter, bake for 17 mins in a gas oven. (Or 2” when a large quantity it desired)

Thank you so much for sharing your family recipe!!! P.S. I so seldom make time to submit a review.

Followed what another reviewer recommended and added the egg to the sour cream mixture along with 1 teaspoon of vanilla. At the end, added orange zest from 2 oranges and 1 cup of dried cranberries (omitted the raisins). Once the scones were cooled drizzled an orange glaze made of 1/2 cup icing sugar, 1 tbsp orange juice, and 1/2 tsp orange zest over the scones. Next time if using a glaze on the scones would reduce the sugar in the scone recipe to 3/4 cup so that they don't get too sweet with a glaze added to them.

These scones are amazing. Some tips - the butter needs to be COLD. I use a food processor to cut mine into the flour (put about half the flour/sugar mix into the processor, slice up all the butter into 1tbsp chunks and add them to the flour, then pulse until butter is cut in to desired size). Also, once you add the sour cream and egg, if the mixture seems TOO dry or crumbly, press it into a big mound in the bowl and let it rest for 3-4 minutes. I generally add toffee or cinnamon chips at this stage, then knead dough to incorporate the chips, then roll out.

I have made these so many times now and each and every they come out perfect- so tender! My husband never cared for scones until I started making these…. Now they are a staple for when we are traveling in our RV. They freeze so well (I wrap them individually in wax paper & place in a freezer bag) and the recipe lends itself to all kinds of variations. This time I did lemon with dark chocolate, but lemon blueberry, cranberry dark chocolate, and orange cranberry are already favorites. Excellent results from a superb recipe!

These always get rave reviews! I use a 6 oz bag of craisins and 2 tbs of grated orange peel instead of raisins for cranberry orange scones. I also separate the dough into 4 equal balls and then roll each out and cut each into 8 mini scones.

I make this recipe about every two weeks. I make them with dried cranberries, chocolate chips, or raisins. I make them 44 of triangles instead of 12. Less calories. I haven't found anyone that hasn't enjoyed them. They do stop a sweet tooth craving.

This recipe is amazing and delicious!!! The scones were soft and fluffy and wonderful! I added currants, raisins, and dried orange peel.
I followed a couple of suggestions in the reviews:
1. I beat in a tablespoon of vanilla with the egg before adding it to the flour mixture. 
2. I rolled the dough into 16 balls and slightly flattened them.

I followed the directions in the FEB/MAR 2020 edition of the printed magazine - 400 degrees, and I used dried blueberries. I brushed them with cream and sprinkled with raw cane turbinado sugar. My wife commented that they were much better than the ones I usually make - I agree. Best scones I've ever had.

Instead of cream of tartar, I used doubled the amount of lemon juice as a substitute. Replaced the raisins for semi-sweet chocolate chips. Added 1 tsp of vanilla to the beaten egg. Kept the thickness at on inch and baked for the full 15 minutes. Turned out fabulous.

I cut the recipe in half. At first, I didn't like cutting in the butter late (after adding sour cream mixture). The dough was so sticky! I struggled then to cut the butter in well. However, these are the tastiest, moistest, scones ever! I also was one tbsp short of butter, so I added a tablespoon of shortening, which resulted in crispy edges. Yum.

I made these for a friend who came from the moors of England. I asked him if they used raisins and he said no. They turned out perfect. I think they taste like biscuits. I made Dorchester cream for a topping. They are very good with the cream and strawberry jam. I can see from the comments that it's easy to make variations.
I have made these for years. They are so many ways to flavor them.

These are awesome. The first time I made them as written, but without the raisins, and everyone thought they tasted like tea cakes. I thought so too. After that I’ve been trying different variations and they always turn out perfect. Try this recipe and you won’t be sorry.

These were not good scones. They had an overwhelming taste of flour and lacked a good scone texture. I'm an advanced home baker and followed the instructions down to the tee but these ended up in the garbage. Disappointed
Raspberries with white chocolate chips is a favorite! Also cinnamon chips with cinnamon added to the batter

I have been making this recipe for 15 years. I use a large cut up chocolate candy bar like Hersheys Symphony instead of raisins. The scones turn out best if they are thick. Frozen berries are good too but can be messy.
